resources.string:
AtlayaSwitch works best with three separate GrapheneOS profiles:

• Owner – the system profile (User 0). Device management, developer options and Shizuku run here; only visible in this profile.

• Private – your everyday profile for daily work, with all the apps and accounts you normally need.

• Away – a decoy profile with believable but unremarkable everyday content (e.g. a few harmless photos, unremarkable apps like camera, maps, weather) instead of real accounts or data. Completely empty looks suspicious – it should look like the phone of someone with nothing to hide.

This separation is the core of the duress concept, a graduated response: in an emergency, AtlayaSwitch immediately and quietly switches from the active profile to the harmless "Away" profile – no password prompt, no visible menu. That's usually enough. Only if you decide yourself that more is needed (for example, if someone finds out there are further profiles), GrapheneOS offers its own last-resort feature, the duress PIN: it destroys the encryption permanently and irrecoverably. AtlayaSwitch neither triggers it nor replaces it – that decision is entirely yours.

WARNING: AtlayaSwitch is installed in the target profile \"%1$s\" itself. The target profile is meant to stay unremarkable (even to third parties, e.g. during a check) – having AtlayaSwitch installed there reveals that a hidden switching mechanism exists. Please remove it.
Removal failed – please check manually: Settings → Apps → AtlayaSwitch → uninstall in profile \"%1$s\".
Switches to the target profile; the previous profile stays active and unlocked in the background.

After switching, also fully ends the previous profile (its apps are closed, GrapheneOS removes its encryption keys from RAM/hardware registers – the profile goes back \"at rest\") – default. Note: when switching from the \"Owner\" profile, Android may refuse this, since the system user can never be stopped – in that case it silently just switches, with no error message.

Shizuku is not installed – the profile switch won\'t work without it. Best installed from the Play Store; then tap \"Open Shizuku\" here and set up \"Start via Wireless debugging\" once (runs entirely on the device, no PC needed).
Shizuku is not installed. Developer options and Wireless debugging are only visible in the \"Owner\" profile – install and set it up there first, it will then be detected here automatically.

Shizuku is installed but not running (e.g. after a device restart) – required for the profile switch. Without a PC: in Developer options switch on USB debugging (it stays on) and Wireless debugging, then tap \"Start via Wireless debugging\" in Shizuku. AtlayaSwitch then switches Wireless debugging off again by itself.

Shizuku isn\'t running and can\'t be started from here: Developer options/Wireless debugging are only visible in the \"Owner\" profile. Open it there and tap \"Start via Wireless debugging\" once – it will then keep running system-wide, including here.

Wireless debugging is only needed to start Shizuku after a restart (no PC required). Once Shizuku is running it can stay off – that closes an open network entry point. AtlayaSwitch then switches it off itself. Requirement: USB debugging stays on (works without a cable or PC), otherwise Android stops the debugging service and Shizuku with it.

⚠ Security trade-off: Shizuku can only be started through Android\'s debugging service (adbd). Developer options and USB debugging therefore have to stay on permanently, and Wireless debugging briefly after every restart. That is more attack surface than a device without it – if you chose GrapheneOS for exactly that reason, weigh this app carefully. AtlayaSwitch turns Wireless debugging off again after the start. It cannot turn USB debugging off: with both off, Android stops the service and Shizuku with it. Remaining risk: a computer authorised once with “Always allow” stays a standing key. Only authorise your own, secured computer, use “Revoke USB debugging authorisations” if unsure, and enable GrapheneOS Auto reboot.
Switch off automatically after Shizuku has started (recommended)
Wireless debugging was switched off. Shizuku keeps running.

Wireless debugging is still on and was NOT switched off: USB debugging is off – Android would otherwise stop the debugging service and Shizuku with it. In the \"Owner\" profile, switch on USB debugging first (no cable or PC needed), then reopen this page.
Wireless debugging could not be switched off – please switch it off manually in Developer options.

Replaces the earlier NFC trigger: tapping a tile in the Quick Settings panel triggers the same switch as the app icon tap – even from the lock screen, without opening the app. Unlike the app icon tap, the tile is visible in the pulled-down panel (icon/name kept deliberately neutral). Add the tile in the panel yourself via the pencil/edit icon afterwards.
